knowledge_point.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression

question.:question/worked-solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int xe^{- 5 x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′} & =e^{- 5 x}\, & ⟹\,v=- \frac{e^{- 5 x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot e^{- 5 x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \left(- \frac{e^{- 5 x}}{5}\right)-\int \left(- \frac{e^{- 5 x}}{5}\right)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{1}{5}\cdot xe^{- 5 x}+\frac{1}{5}\cdot \int e^{- 5 x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int xe^{- 5 x}\,\text{d}x & =- \frac{1}{5}\cdot xe^{- 5 x}+\frac{1}{5}\cdot \int e^{- 5 x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{1}{5}\cdot xe^{- 5 x}-\frac{1}{25}\cdot e^{- 5 x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Collecting the linear terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int xe^{- 5 x}\,\mathrm{d}x & =-\frac{x e^{- 5 x}}{5} - \frac{e^{- 5 x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$
